newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong's Hang Seng squeaks to new record close.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong's Hang Seng squeaks to new record close.

text.p: Hong Kong's Hang Seng index squeaked to a new record close on Tuesday, after a mixed session buoyed by late European interest and some laggard chasing, traders said.
The Hang Seng index closed 34.45 points higher at 12,806.31. The previous record close was on November 6 at 12,775.47.
Turnover was HK$6.88 billion compared with Monday's HK$6.41 billion.
"The fact we picked up in the second half would suggest that we are seeing some buying from the Europeans," said Miles Remington, sales trader at Crosby Securities.
He said buyers had focused on lagging stocks and China infrastructure plays, offsetting weakness in the utility sector.

"It was a mixed market all day," said Glenn Lesko, head of sales trading HG Asia. "I think lately there has been a rotation into laggards in the property sector. Property investment companies have been sort of the flavour," he said.
Selling pressure in the utility sector helped push the Hang Seng index to a session low of 12,731.27 on Tuesday.
China Light finished the session down HK$1.30 at HK$33.70 following a government request that the company delay the expansion of the Black Point power plant.
HongKong Telecom closed HK$0.25 lower at HK$13.45 after rising on Monday on speculation Cable and Wireless would sell part of its stake to a Chinese partner.
However, property investment firms Hysan and Amoy advanced. Hysan rose HK$0.55 to HK$26.85 and Amoy rose HK$0.15 to HK$9.95.
Among the China infrastructure plays, Kerry Properties gained HK$1.25 to HK$21.95 and Cheung Kong Infrastructure rose HK$0.20 to HK$15.45.
"Buying this afternoon was particularly attracted by China infrastructure plays, all of which are reacting to stronger than expected earnings from Road King," said Remington.
Among other strong gainers, Hutchison advanced HK$1.00 to HK$57.50 and Hang Seng Bank added HK$1.00 to HK$95.00.
Lesko said Wednesday's government land auction in Hong Kong and the U.S. Federal Reserve meeting, also on Wednesday, could both help the market.

"If you look back over the last few months, both of those have turned out to be very positive events for the market," he said. "As we get closer and closer to some of these events tomorrow, sentiment does seem to be picking up."
